How to fill it in

How a good monthly report is built

A management report should answer a question: are we on track, and what must someone decide? It should say so on the first page, back it up with a few charts, and list owners and dates for the next steps. This template follows that order. Because the numbers live in a CSV and the sentences refer to them by name, the text cannot say 2% when the chart says 4%.

Step 1: Look at the CSV

Open monthly-kpi-report-template-data.csv in Excel, Google Sheets or a text editor. It has one row per month and one column per metric: month as YYYY-MM, then revenue, gross margin, new customers, churn, CAC and cash. Percentages are plain numbers, so 62.4 means 62.4%. Replace the sample rows with yours. Include at least the reporting month and the previous one, and ideally twelve months so the charts have a trend.

Step 2: Look at the notes file

The notes file is plain text. The top lines name the company, report title, period, currency and who prepared it. The Metrics section lists each metric with its label, format, whether up or down is good and the target. The rest is the text of the report. Numbers in the text are written as tokens such as {revenue} and {revenue.vs_target}, which are filled from the CSV when the report is built.

Step 3: Decide the headline before you write

Ask: what is the one thing the reader needs to know this month? Write that as a verdict, for example “Revenue is behind plan because churn rose”. Avoid titles such as “Revenue update”. If you do not know the cause of a change, say “cause to be confirmed” rather than invent a reason. Keep to three key points and four to six metrics.

Step 4: Set targets and risks

Give each metric a target for the reporting month, or the report will have nothing to compare against. List two or three risks with an owner and a mitigation, and next steps with an owner and a date. If you do not know an owner, ask before you publish; an action with no owner is a wish.

Step 5: Rebuild the PDF

The PDF is produced by the free monthly-kpi-report skill, a Python script that reads these two files. If you are comfortable with Python, run it yourself; the KPI report guide explains each step. If not, the PDF still shows exactly what a good report looks like, and you can recreate the layout in your own tool, or ask a coding agent to run the skill for you.

Step 6: Make it a routine

Next month, add one row to the CSV, change the period line, update targets if they moved and rewrite only the judgement parts. Check every page before sending: no clipped text, the arrows show bad moves for lower-is-better metrics such as churn, and every figure in the text agrees with the appendix.

Common mistakes to avoid

Too many metrics, no targets and no owners are the three most common failures of monthly reports. If the first page has fourteen tiles, nobody knows which one matters. If there are no targets, a number cannot be good or bad. If next steps have no owner and date, they will not happen. Also watch for definitions that drift: if “churn” means something different this quarter, say so on the page. Keep the same definitions month to month so the trend means something.

Frequently asked questions

Is this KPI report template free?

Yes. All three files are free to download and use.

Can I edit the PDF?

The PDF is the finished example. You change the CSV and notes file and rebuild with the free skill. You can also copy its structure into Word, Slides or your own reporting tool.

Which metrics should I put in?

Four to six that someone will act on. The sample uses revenue, gross margin, new customers, churn, CAC and cash. Replace them with your own.

Does it use real data?

No. Everything in the sample is fictional.
